findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk error)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? instead of unwrap

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) performs console I/O inside load_sessions, which is a data-loading function that should be pure
findings.failure_mode: side-effectful logging in a core data function makes it impossible to test deterministically and couples domain logic to stdout
findings.fix: remove println! from load_sessions; move logging to the caller/shell layer after loading completes

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked array indexing without bounds verification
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with zero fields causes a panic at runtime via out-of-bounds access
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and handle None with a typed error or skip

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() creates a full Vec allocation to access two fields, violating the split_once rule
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation for every line; also makes it easy to index unsafely on subsequent fields
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to extract name and remainder, then parse remainder for value without collecting all parts

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input and on missing second field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (non-numeric value or missing field) aborts the program instead of returning a parse/validation error
findings.fix: use parts.get(1) with ? propagation, then parse with .map_err() to return a typed ParseError, never unwrap

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16, silently truncating values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a value like 70000 parses successfully as u32 then truncates to 4444 when cast to u16, producing incorrect data with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) or parse directly as u16, propagating error via map_err on Infallible

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no try_reserve for bounded capacity pre-allocation
findings.failure_mode: unknown line count causes repeated reallocations as the Vec grows, degrading performance and wasting memory
findings.fix: estimate capacity, compute with checked_mul, and call Vec::try_reserve; handle Allocation error by returning Result

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for the I/O-bound load_sessions function
findings.failure_mode: performance claims (or regressions) for file loading cannot be measured or tracked
findings.fix: add a criterion or similar benchmark measuring throughput and memory allocations for typical input sizes

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or memory allocations
no profiler data for I/O-bound path
no allocation tracing (e.g., mimalloc profiler or similar) for Vec growth behavior
no CLI command harness or exit-code contract documented for load_sessions usage
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. All six BLOCKER violations (unwrap/panic on I/O and parse, unchecked indexing, lossy as cast, I/O side effect in core, unnecessary split+collect) require immediate repair before any delivery gate. The function as-written will panic on missing files, malformed lines, and oversized values.
